original_query: with customer_total_return as (select sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk ,sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk ,sum(SR_STORE_CREDIT) as ctr_total_return from store_returns ,date_dim where sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year =2000 and sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity between 107 and 166 group by sr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk)  select  c_customer_id from customer_total_return ctr1 ,store ,customer ,customer_demographics where ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk ) and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 17 AND 20 and s_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk and s_state IN ('MO', 'NC', 'PA') and ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and cd_marital_status IN ('D', 'W') and cd_education_status IN ('College', 'Unknown') and cd_gender = 'F' and c_birth_month = 5 and c_birth_year BETWEEN 1956 AND 1962 order by c_customer_id limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH customer_total_return AS (
    SELECT sr.sr_customer_sk AS ctr_customer_sk,
           sr.sr_store_sk AS ctr_store_sk,
           sr.sr_reason_sk AS ctr_reason_sk,
           SUM(sr.sr_store_credit) AS ctr_total_return
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN date_dim d ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN store s ON s.s_store_sk = sr.sr_store_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2000
      AND sr.sr_return_amt / sr.sr_return_quantity BETWEEN 107 AND 166
      AND s.s_state IN ('MO', 'NC', 'PA')
    GROUP BY sr.sr_customer_sk, sr.sr_store_sk, sr.sr_reason_sk
),
store_avg AS (
    SELECT ctr_store_sk,
           AVG(ctr_total_return) * 1.2 AS avg_threshold
    FROM customer_total_return
    GROUP BY ctr_store_sk
)
SELECT c.c_customer_id
FROM customer_total_return ctr
JOIN store_avg sa ON ctr.ctr_store_sk = sa.ctr_store_sk
JOIN customer c ON c.c_customer_sk = ctr.ctr_customer_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
WHERE ctr.ctr_total_return > sa.avg_threshold
  AND ctr.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 17 AND 20
  AND cd.cd_marital_status IN ('D', 'W')
  AND cd.cd_education_status IN ('College', 'Unknown')
  AND cd.cd_gender = 'F'
  AND c.c_birth_month = 5
  AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1956 AND 1962
ORDER BY c.c_customer_id
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated subquery (per-row AVG over customer_total_return ctr2) with a pre-aggregated store_avg CTE computing AVG(ctr_total_return)*1.2 once per store, then join. This eliminates repeated CTE scans per outer row and improves scalability (score 8/10).

Push the highly selective store filter s_state IN ('MO','NC','PA') into the customer_total_return CTE by joining store before aggregation. Since store state is constant per store_sk, the per-store average is unchanged, while rows scanned/grouped can drop dramatically (store table only 102 rows, ~3/102 states selected) (score 9/10).

Convert implicit comma joins into explicit INNER JOINs. After pushing the store filter into the CTE, the outer store join becomes redundant and is removed; customer and customer_demographics remain as join predicates in the main query.

The AVG(...)*1.2 threshold is folded into the store_avg CTE so multiplication happens once per store rather than per comparison; d_year=2000 and reason/customer literal filters are kept as constant predicates.
